newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures ease slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures ease slightly lower.

text.p: IPE June Brent futures were slightly lower in early trade on Thursday, brokers said.
June Brent was three cents a barrel lower at $17.78 by 1052 GMT after having hit a low of $17.70 earlier while May gas oil was was 50 cents a tonne off at $162.25.
Brokers said sentiment remained soft after Wednesday's heavy losses prompted by rising U.S. stocks and weak gasoline demand.
"I think the weakness in Brent is going to pull gas oil lower," one said. Gas oil dipped on the back of Brent's late losses on Wednesday.
June Brent shed 33 cents to close near session lows at $17.81 a barrel. May gas oil closed $2.75 a tonne lower at $162.50.

Industry and government data showed U.S. stocks of crude, middle distillates and gasoline all rose last week and the American Petroleum Institute said on Wednesday gasoline supply should more than match peak driving season demand this summer.
Both Brent and gas oil fell on Wednesday as some fund selling set into the market, one broker added.
Some brokers said physical gas oil remained well supported in Europe after recent shipments to the Far East.

News of a gas leak overnight at Tosco Corp's 104,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery in Rodeo, California, which forced the company to scale back throughput at some units, was seen providing limited mild support.

"In the short term the market looks oversold and it's possible it's ready for a bounce...So it may well provide (support) but its going to be more of a U.S. issue, so they may use that news plus the fact that the market has pipped off a bit to buy," one broker said.
"There's a good chance that it (Brent) could bounce, it is looking oversold," he added.
But Brent was still close to recent lows around $17.65 with support at $17.72 and resistance in the $17.78 to $17.80 range with crucial resistance set at $18.05, the broker said.
